analysis.investment_thesis: CapitalNumbers is a debt-free, high-ROE IT services small-cap with promoter holding at 74.67% and trading at a modest P/E of 8.91, but IT consulting is outside my circle of competence and revenue growth has nearly stalled (98→100 Cr in FY24→25). The quality of the balance sheet is real, but this is not a consumer compounder I would concentrate in.
key_strengths: Debt-free balance sheet (borrowings 0 Cr) with equity 171 Cr and ROCE 26.5%
key_risks: Revenue growth collapsed to ~2% in FY25 (98→100 Cr) — operating profit also contracted from 34 to 30 Cr
IT services to global startups is cyclical and discretionary — not predictable consumer demand
Recent large equity infusion (reserves jumped 46→147 Cr, investing CF -77 Cr) — capital allocation on unproven deployment
red_flags: Sudden equity raise of ~100 Cr in FY25 parked in investing outflows — returns on this capital unproven
Operating CF dipped from 22 to 19 Cr despite flat revenue — margin pressure emerging
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my lens, the financial hygiene is genuinely good: zero borrowings across recent years, ROE of 20%, ROCE of 26.5%, 5/5 years positive OCF, and promoters holding a committed 74.67%. P/E of 8.91 with a 5-year profit CAGR of 39% looks cheap on paper, and this is the kind of quiet, under-followed small-cap I sometimes find interesting. However, I built my conviction in retail because consumer demand is predictable — IT consulting for overseas startups is not. The FY25 slowdown (revenue 98→100 Cr, operating income 34→30 Cr) tells me the global discretionary tech spend cycle is hitting them, and this is exactly the volatility I avoid.

The IPO/QIP-style capital raise in FY25 (equity jumping from 67 to 171 Cr, investing outflows of 77 Cr) concerns me more than the multiple reassures me. Good businesses compound quietly on internal accruals; raising capital before demonstrating how it will earn 20%+ returns is a yellow flag. I would watch for two more years of execution — can revenue growth re-accelerate past 15%, and does the deployed capital earn a reasonable ROCE? Until then, this is a HOLD/watch-list name, not a core position. Not my kind of compounder.
